title: Lesson 2.3 Knowledge Check
description: Five questions on movement prompts, diagnosis, and composition. Unlimited attempts; your best score counts.

questions.text: Which are the five elements of dance used as the prompt frame in this lesson? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: Body, action, space, time, and energy. Costume is a design element, not a movement element.

questions.text: A generated clip shows the dancer with extra limbs and ignores your tempo. According to the three-fix method, what should you try first?
options: Edit the clip to hide the limbs
Revise the prompt: one dancer, one action, one quality, single shot, stated duration
Add a soundtrack to distract from the error
questions.feedback: Most failures come from overloaded prompts. Simplify first; change tools or edit only if that fails.

questions.text: Four generated phrases placed in order with no choreographic device already constitute a composition.
questions.feedback: Composition is the intentional arrangement of phrases with a device such as repetition, canon, contrast, or accumulation. Without it you have a slideshow.

questions.text: Which of these is a choreographic device?
questions.feedback: Canon (the same phrase performed by different bodies at staggered times) is a choreographic device. The others are video settings.

questions.text: Why does the lesson require a transfer note about live rehearsal?
options: Because the goal is live performance; the video is a tool for visualizing and directing movement, not a replacement for bodies in a room
questions.feedback: Every artifact in the theater module returns to the rehearsal room.
